name: hcapp_logAppError
description: Records a client-side error in HC.AppError. The device must be registered in HC.Device (Device.UserId lookup by @deviceId), but the access token is intentionally NOT validated so the app can log errors even when it cannot generate a token — @accessToken is accepted and ignored. No permission gate. Returns the write envelope (success=1) alone on success, or success=0 followed by the error detail on device-not-registered (1392/13) or an unhandled error (1992/19).

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Must resolve to a Device.UserId — the SP's only check. Stored as AppError.DeviceId.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Accepted for API consistency; never validated (by design — see description). Dead input.

parameters.name: httpBody
parameters.description: HTTP request body captured at the time of the error. Optional.

parameters.name: errorText
parameters.description: The error message or exception text. Matches AppError.ErrorText NVARCHAR(1000); longer text is silently truncated at the parameter.

parameters.name: extraData
parameters.description: Additional diagnostic context — JSON, stack trace, free text. Optional.

rowsets.name: StatusEnvelope
rowsets.description: Always the first rowset. success=1: recorded, nothing follows. success=0: rowset 1 carries the detail. 1392/13 device not registered, 1992/19 unhandled.

columns.name: success
columns.description: 1 on insert, 0 on device-not-found or unhandled error.

sideEffects: INSERT HC.AppError (DeviceId, HttpBody, ErrorText, ExtraData) — id and createdAt from table defaults; inside a transaction (lines 62-67)
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on device-not-found (userId NULL, outside the transaction) and on the CATCH path (after ROLLBACK); HcVersion from HC6.DeviceHcVersion(@deviceId)

codeSmells.detail: @deviceId, @accessToken and @errorText (lines 3, 4, 6) have no SQL default. A client that omits one gets an unlogged empty 500 before the body runs — on the one SP whose job is to record that something went wrong.
Deliberate (header, lines 12-16): anyone who knows a registered deviceId can write to HC.AppError without a token. Documented trust trade-off, not an oversight.

@errorText NVARCHAR(1000) (line 6) matches the column width, so an exception message longer than 1000 characters is cut at the parameter with no error rather than refused — the tail of a long stack message is lost.
Line 47: Device.UserId is NULLable, so the NULL check already covers an unassigned device; the zero-UUID comparison is harmless but dead.

breakingChanges: Device existence is now validated — HC5 performed no auth or existence check whatsoever; callers whose @deviceId is not registered in HC.Device will now receive a success=0 error response instead of silently inserting

Response shape changed from a single hardcoded 'Error recorded' rowset (HC5) to the write SP envelope pattern (StatusEnvelope as rowset 0, optional ErrorDetail as rowset 1) — all Flutter callers parsing the HC5 single-rowset response must be updated
TRY/CATCH added — DB errors that previously propagated as unhandled SQL exceptions are now caught and returned as structured error responses
